page: Amazon Web Services z1d.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8151 processor offering a sustained clock frequency of 4.0 GHz across 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via multithreading. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by vector extensions including AVX and AVX-512F. Local high-speed storage is bundled in the form of a 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, accompanied by a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No physical GPUs are present on this machine.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread behavior contrasting with limited multi-core throughput due to the low total core count. The 4.0 GHz clock speed drives average results in single-threaded tests, including a 1652.79 score in stress-ng single-core, a Geekbench single-core score of 1314.0, and 28.05 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, aggregate parallel compute shows low metrics across wider workloads, illustrated by a stress-ng multi-core result of 4342.06 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2868.0. Memory bandwidth aligns with DDR4 characteristics, delivering 27.56 GB/sec for uncached large block reads.

The z1d.xlarge instance trades parallel thread capacity for elevated single-core frequency and a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. This profile suits per-core licensed relational databases, in-memory caches requiring low write latency, and electronic design automation (EDA) where high clock speed accelerates serial execution pipelines while local NVMe storage assists scratch operations.
description: Amazon Web Services z1d.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring a high-frequency Intel Xeon 8151 processor running at 4.0 GHz. The system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a 150 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Network baseline throughput is configured at 1 Gbps, with zero dedicated GPUs. Performance benchmarks show balanced single-core execution—achieving 1314.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1652.79 in stress-ng—contrasted with low multi-core totals driven by the low core count. With 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, z1d.xlarge delivers cost-efficient resource density for workloads bottlenecked by serial frequency or constrained by per-core software licensing, such as relational databases, in-memory data structures, and electronic design automation tasks.
